_policy: Pre-registered targets for the #4402 round (the phase arbiter's quarter-beat candidates), frozen BEFORE any arm was scored live, in the shape of q4234_guard_frozen.json: numbers below are read from the baseline root (the shipped behavior); arms are selected on the TUNE halves and the holdout is read once on the chosen arm.
issue: The phase arbiter folds its events into an on-grid bin and a half-beat bin only (|f| <= 1/8, |f - 1/2| <= 1/8); events a quarter of a beat off count for neither, so a grid that locked a quarter late or early never moves. On today's grid (tune, T-level) that is 9 Ballroom tracks (summed 1-F 7.6 of 344), 1 Harmonix track, and every batida techno render (#3344: the grid sits ~.30 beat late for 30 s at the start and again mid-track, outside the PLL's +-25% capture, with ZERO events on its instants and every event in the 3/4 bin). Grids a third off (5 Ballroom tune tracks, swing 'and' at 2/3) stay out of reach: the beat leads the 'and' ~1.4:1 there and third-beat candidates flip right swing grids (tune forecast Ballroom -.012, batida waltz -.65, techno -.28).
mechanism_evidence: finding to be filed: replay_n.py (replay.py generalized to N offsets) replays the shipped arbiter from the baseline beat sidecar EXACTLY (604 tracks incl. 80 batida, 129,963 votes, 0 mismatches); the knob binary (quarters on) matches the replica's quarter rule exactly on 35 tracks / 8,555 votes (bins, votes, streaks, shift offsets). Tune forecast (replica with a PLL-snap fidelity patch) of the arms: q16 Ballroom +.0072 (+9/-3), Harmonix +.0011 (+3/-3), techno +.089; q24 +.0063 (+9/-3) / +.0002 (+3/-3) / +.086; q24r3 +.0051 (+5/-2) / +.0009 (+2/-2) / +.084. Live knob binary vs forecast on the 35 most-moved tune tracks + techno: 25/35 within .1 beat F, 32/35 in the forecast's direction; live Ballroom summed gain +3.71 vs forecast +2.45 (the live PLL recovers most forecast losses), techno +1.01 vs +.89, Harmonix +.06 = +.06. The one large live loss is 0713_heartofgoldnow .99 -> .28 (an intro figure puts every event a quarter early for a bar while the grid is right). Without a long-window minimum every quarter rule loses on Harmonix (the first-bar-after-lock votes); act-only evidence is worse (Ballroom -.012 to -.022).
design_constraint: The shipped half-beat rule runs first and unchanged (same bins, ratio, guard, streak); the quarter candidates (1/4, 3/4; tolerance 1/8, the shipped one) are consulted only at an instant where it abstains, so the arbiter is a strict superset of the shipped one (unit test: identical beats on the half-beat scenarios). A quarter vote needs the fuller quarter bin to beat the on-grid bin by q_ratio in the 8-beat window, the 32-beat window to agree (shipped 1.5:1 and .4 share) and to hold at least q_long_min events, and q_dom x the runner-up bin when set; a shift moves the grid LATER by the offset (never a double beat). Evidence streams, event threshold, PLL, estimator and scheduler stay as shipped; the arbiter does not feed the tempo estimator, so tempo metrics are identical by construction (G1) and the wire's published bpm cannot change (G5 publish).
